quick_skim.title: Schizophrenia Detection from EEG Signals: A Transformer Framework with Spectrogram Representation
quick_skim.abstract: Schizophrenia is a serious psychiatric disorder that affects millions of people worldwide, and its diagnosis remains primarily dependent on clinical assessment. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive approach to investigate brain activity and has shown potential to support automated Schizophrenia detection. However, existing EEG-based classification studies often suffer from limitations including small datasets, inconsistent preprocessing strategies, and evaluation protocols that may not adequately prevent subject-related data leakage. In this study, we propose an EEG-based Schizophrenia classification framework that transforms preprocessed EEG recordings into time-frequency representations using the Short-Time Fourier Transform. The generated spectrogram images are classified using both conventional Machine Learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, and XGBoost, and Deep Learning models, including convolutional architectures and CNN-Transformer hybrids. To ensure reliable evaluation, all data partitions are performed at the subject level. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves competitive classification performance, with the CNN-Transformer (CT-SZ) model achieving an AUC-ROC of 88.41% and the CNN + Squeeze and Excitation + Transformer (CST-SZ) achieving an AUC-ROC of 92.88% on the independent test set.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: EEG-based AI detection of a brain disorder
quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: An EEG-based Transformer framework converts recordings into spectrogram time-frequency representations to detect schizophrenia automatically, addressing small datasets and evaluation leakage in prior EEG classification studies.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对精神分裂症诊断主要依赖临床评估、EEG自动分类研究常受小样本与评估泄漏困扰的问题，本文提出基于Transformer的EEG分类框架，将预处理脑电信号转换为短时傅里叶时频表征后建模。实验表明该框架能有效区分精神分裂症患者与对照，并强调无泄漏的评估协议。该工作为脑电信号驱动的精神疾病自动辅助诊断提供了可复现的深度学习方法。

quick_skim.title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models
quick_skim.abstract: EEG foundation models such as BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGMamba have achieved remarkable performance in neural signal decoding, but their black-box nature limits clinical trust and neuroscientific validation. We propose a unified attribution framework for interpreting EEG foundation models across heterogeneous architectures. The framework integrates gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based explanation methods to analyze model behavior in spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions. Spatially, it identifies critical EEG channels and visualizes their distributions using topographic maps. Temporally, it highlights decision-relevant signal segments through attribution heatmaps. In the frequency domain, it quantifies the contributions of canonical EEG rhythms via spectral perturbation analysis. To assess explanation reliability, we introduce a population-level evaluation combining Area Over the Perturbation Curve (AOPC) and cross-method consistency analysis. The framework further leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to transform structured attribution outputs into natural-language reports, bridging low-level neural representations and high-level semantic reasoning. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including Mumtaz2016 and TUAB, demonstrate that the generated explanations are consistent with established neurophysiological markers, validating meaningful neural representations while exposing potential dependencies on artifacts and spurious patterns. The proposed framework provides a standardized approach for evaluating the interpretability, reliability, and physiological plausibility of EEG foundation models.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: interpretability for EEG foundation models in clinical neuro-signal decoding
quick_skim.llm_evidence_cn: 面向EEG基础模型的临床神经信号解码可解释性
quick_skim.llm_evidence: 面向EEG基础模型的临床神经信号解码可解释性
quick_skim.canonical_evidence: 面向EEG基础模型的临床神经信号解码可解释性
quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: EEG foundation models decode neural signals well but remain black boxes, limiting clinical trust. EEG-Xplain unifies gradient, perturbation and activation attributions to analyze model behavior across spatial, temporal and frequency dimensions of EEG.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: EEG基础模型在神经信号解码上表现优异，但其黑箱特性限制了临床信任与神经科学验证。本文提出EEG-Xplain统一归因框架，整合梯度、扰动与激活类解释方法，从空间、时间、频率三个维度分析模型行为，识别关键EEG通道、决策相关信号段与节律贡献。该工作为异构EEG基础模型提供了可解释性分析工具，推动神经影像AI在临床中的可信应用。
